subject: National literals
notes: cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.3 "any character in the national coded character set that the implementor has designated for source code representation" -> OK (rule 2). STR_BODY admits every character except the delimiter and CR/LF; source text is read as UTF-8 so both dashes hold: an ASCII (alphanumeric-set) character and a character outside Latin-1 are each stored as one national (UTF-16) position. Probe p1: N"\u00e9\u6f22" MOVE/DISPLAY exact, LENGTH(N"\u00e9x")=2. The character set designation itself is Annex A.1 item 31 (documentation owned by that DOC row). [editions as adjudicated: COBOL-2002, COBOL-2014, COBOL-2023 (national literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; absent from COBOL-85, where the construct is rejected COBOL0900 via Constructs.NationalData2002)]
